Connecting Canada to markets across Europe 🇨🇦 🇪🇺

At MSC, we offer regular connections from Canada to destinations from Northern Europe to the Mediterranean and beyond.

With weekly sailings, bi-weekly sailings from Montreal and extensive inland solutions on both sides of the Atlantic, our network gives customers the flexibility to find the connections that best fit their cargo and supply chain needs.

In Europe, key gateways include Antwerp, Bremerhaven and Gioia Tauro, providing onward access to markets from Ireland and ScanBalt to the Adriatic, Black Sea and East Mediterranean.

Meanwhile, our all-water connection via Vancouver provides another option for cargo moving from Canada to Europe.

With heavy hearts, we bid farewell to Captain Pasquale Formisano.

Pasquale was one of the pioneers who helped build MSC from its earliest years. In the early 1970s, he worked alongside our founder, Captain Gianluigi Aponte, as MSC began to grow, and accompanied the first MSC vessel to call at Antwerp.

Over the decades that followed, Pasquale became one of the most recognised and respected figures in the shipping industry. His extraordinary dedication to MSC and deep knowledge of shipping earned him enormous respect from customers, partners, colleagues and peers around the world.

But for those who knew him, Pasquale was much more than that. A man of strong principles and strong character, he was straightforward, hardworking and generous, with an unmistakable sense of humour and a big heart. He was always there to help friends and colleagues.

Pasquale was truly one of a kind, and his loss leaves a great void for all of us who had the privilege of knowing him. But the mark he left on our company, our industry and so many people will remain.

Our deepest sympathies are with his family and loved ones at this very sad time.

Buon vento, caro Pasquale. ⚓

From Antwerp to Alexandria – moving railcars for Cairo’s metro 🚆⚓️

In this video, Mohamed Emad, Export Trade & Project Cargo Manager at MSC Egypt, takes us behind the scenes of a complex project cargo operation in the Port of Antwerp. Here, a complete trainset of nine railcars is loaded for its journey to Egypt on MSC’s Levante Express service.

Each railcar weighs up to 40 tonnes and measures up to 22 metres. With the cargo shipped unpacked, every step demands precision, specific sequencing and experienced hands. The railcars are carefully lashed and secured to ensure they are ready for their journey to Alexandria.

Once in Egypt, the trainset will be used for the Cairo metro, helping transport around 2.5 million passengers every day.

Moving a stacker reclaimer from India to Belgium ⚓️ 🏗️

In Ennore, Rahul Singh, Senior Manager Project Cargo at MSC India, walks us through the loading of a stacker reclaimer bound for Antwerp.

The cargo is a large machine used to handle bulk materials such as coal, iron ore, or grain. Due to its size, up to 8 metres wide, it is shipped as 9 dismantled units.

To support the load, 36 flat racks (40’) are arranged across 4 bays, creating an artificial twin deck to safely position and secure the cargo on board.

Once lashed and secured, the shipment is ready for its journey to Antwerp on our Australia Express service.

Due to the evolving security situation in the Middle East and the restrictions affecting maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, MSC has taken precautionary measures to safeguard its crews and operations.

All MSC vessels currently operating in the Gulf region, as well as those en route, have been instructed to proceed to designated safe shelter areas until further notice.

In addition, MSC has temporarily suspended all bookings for worldwide cargo to the Middle East region. Bookings will resume as soon as the security situation improves.

We continue to closely monitor developments and are working with the relevant authorities.

Customers will be informed as soon as further details become available, including any potential alternative discharge ports should additional operational adjustments be required.

Extra care for food and pharmaceutical shipments 🛡️❄️⚓

On 28 April 2026, MSC and MEDLOG Transport & Logistics received renewed certifications for their FSM and GDP protocols from RINA, a leading certification body. It reflects our commitment to the highest standards of cargo safety and customer care.

For our customers, this means greater control and reliability. By opting for a GDP- or FSM-certified solution, they benefit from additional services such as compliance protocols, 24/7 monitoring and end-of-trip reporting.

For even more control, these solutions can be combined with MSC iReefer, our advanced container monitoring system for refrigerated cargo.

At MSC, we have been very clear about where we stand on Arctic shipping. The Arctic is not a shortcut.

As we have stated before, we do not use the Northern Sea Route. The environmental, safety and operational risks in such a fragile and remote region are simply too great. Read more about our position here: https://lnkd.in/eTrTi7Vz

This article from Blueconomy.com places our position in a broader context. It highlights the growing geopolitical pressure on the Arctic, the lack of supporting infrastructure, and the environmental consequences of increased commercial traffic in the region.
